review.intent_summary: Explicit reset boundaries let each regime establish its own baseline, trend, and calibration after a known change.

criteria.criterion: Integer positions and exact observed dates or timestamps can identify reset boundaries.
Each new regime rebuilds its reference, trend, and calibration without crossing earlier boundaries.
Repeated, out-of-range, or unmatched reset points are rejected.
criteria.notes: Standard validation rejects invalid boundaries, but sparse analysis with as_of silently filters some invalid resets before validation. Reproduced acceptance of position 999 and unmatched date 2099-01-01 against a 14-sample series.

criteria.criterion: CLI reset options produce the same resolved positions and suppress departures explained by the declared boundaries.

verification_evidence: Inspected examples/steps_reset.json through analyze(): resolved positions [50, 100], three calibrated segments with separate training/calibration windows, zero observations and patterns.
Direct resolver checks passed for offset-normalized exact timestamps and duplicate/unmatched timestamp rejection.
Confirmed sparse analysis with as_of accepts invalid reset position 999 and unmatched date 2099-01-01, resolving both to no boundaries.
remaining_gaps: Validate invalid reset declarations before sparse as_of filtering while preserving deferred valid boundaries; add focused regression coverage.
